delete.description:
Soft-delete (sets deleted_at). Engagements still reference the family
via ON DELETE RESTRICT, so the row stays — the deleted_at filter just
hides it from listings.

Detach the person from the family. The person row stays in
`people` (and any audit_log entries referencing this id remain
valid); only the family_guardians junction row is removed. If
you want to fully remove the person from the address book,
soft-delete via people.deleted_at — a future endpoint.

Soft delete: sets people.deleted_at. The student disappears
from listings and detail. family_students and student_details rows
remain so audit_log entries and engagements still reference a real
person; the engagements.student_id FK is ON DELETE RESTRICT, so
a hard-delete with active engagements would fail anyway.

Soft delete (sets deleted_at). Visits/recommendations reference
schools via ON DELETE RESTRICT, so the row stays intact — the
deleted_at filter just hides it from listings.

schema.title: School Filter

schema.description: When set, contacts at this school sort first, then unaffiliated, then contacts at other schools. Used by the school-visit attendee typeahead so picks at the visiting school land at the top.
schema.title: Prefer School Id

parameters.description: When set, contacts at this school sort first, then unaffiliated, then contacts at other schools. Used by the school-visit attendee typeahead so picks at the visiting school land at the top.

delete.description:
Soft delete (sets deleted_at). school_visit_attendees references contacts
via ON DELETE RESTRICT so the row stays — the deleted_at filter hides it.

post.description:
Dedicated status-change endpoint — kept separate from PATCH so the
SPA's status-pill control hits a clearly auditable action.

Dedicated status transition endpoint — completed_at is auto-stamped
on the 'done' transition and cleared on any other transition.

delete.description:
Refuses to delete an entry that's already on an invoice — that
invoice's totals are derived from this row and silently mutating
them is bad UX. Void or edit the invoice instead.

get.description:
Datalist hints; the schema doesn't enforce these so they're just a
convenience for the SPA's autocomplete.

delete.description:
Hard delete; the school_visit_attendees rows cascade away via
ON DELETE CASCADE on that join table.

post.description:
Idempotent upsert keyed by (engagement_id, school_id) — repeated
POSTs with the same school don't create duplicates, they update.
Mirrors hillco-portal's ON CONFLICT shape.

get.description:
Phases + service items applicable to this engagement's type, used
by the SPA's "seed the plan" UI. assessment engagements see scope =
'assessment' phases; full_placement engagements see both scopes.

Tasks for an engagement, sorted by their snapshotted phase order
then by per-phase sort_order. Tasks with no phase (ad-hoc) come last.

post.description:
Snapshot the selected service_items into engagement_tasks. Idempotent
per (engagement_id, service_item_id) — already-seeded items are skipped
so calling this again to add newly-checked items is safe.

Dedicated transition; auto-stamps completed_at on 'completed' and
clears it on any other status.

One learning profile per engagement (UNIQUE(engagement_id) at the
DB level). The student is implied by the engagement, so the request
body doesn't carry student_id.

Stamp finalized_at = NOW(). Idempotent — subsequent calls just
refresh the timestamp.

Clears finalized_at. Useful when reopening a profile for revisions
after the family meeting.

Creates an active record. Existing active records of the same
type for the same student would conflict with the partial UNIQUE
index — the route doesn't auto-expire the old one; that's a
deliberate two-step (PATCH old to status='expired', then POST new)
so the operator pauses to think about the transition.

delete.description:
Hard delete. Unlike agreements, learning supports have no
supersession chain to corrupt and no financial weight; deletion is
the right verb for "this was added in error." Use status='expired'
or 'terminated' to retain history.

get.description: List phases with their item counts. Filter by scope when set.

delete.description:
Soft delete. Phase rows still exist so engagement_tasks.phase_id
snapshots stay readable; the deleted_at filter just hides them from
the catalog UI. Active service_items still pointing at the phase
will block hard deletes (RESTRICT FK), but soft delete is safe.

Soft delete. engagement_tasks.service_item_id is ON DELETE SET NULL
so existing tasks keep their snapshots; the catalog just stops
surfacing this item for new selection.

get.description:
Typeahead helper for the upload UI — surfaces families, students,
schools, and engagements whose names match the query.

Family docs + every active student in the family's docs, with a
source_label so the UI can group/label them.

Engagement docs + family docs + every student-on-the-engagement's
docs, with a source_label.

Stream the object through the app instead of redirecting to a
presigned S3 URL. Keeps every read inside the app's audit perimeter,
avoids leaking the URL into browser history/Referer, and lets us add
a documents.read audit row in one place later.

Lists invoices and a financial summary across all engagements.
Status filter:
  - open: sent + overdue
  - paid: only paid
  - draft / void: literal status match
  - all: everything (still excludes deleted)

Billable time entries + expenses on this engagement that aren't
yet attached to an invoice. Powers the SPA's "new invoice" picker.

patch.description:
Edit issue_date / due_date / tax / notes on a draft. Sent/paid/void
invoices are immutable here — that's intentional, mutating a sent
invoice would silently change what the family was billed.

delete.description:
Soft delete; only allowed on drafts. Frees the source time /
expense rows the same way void does.

post.description: Add a 'custom' line — not derived from a time entry or expense.

delete.description:
Drops the line and frees the source time entry / expense back to
the uninvoiced pool when applicable.

post.description:
Records full payment. Partial payments aren't supported — that
would require a second 'amount remaining' concept and a more
careful 'overdue' calculation.

Voids draft/sent/overdue invoices and frees their source time /
expense rows back to the uninvoiced pool. Refusing to void paid
invoices is intentional — that path needs an explicit refund flow
rather than the implicit free-and-rebill that would happen here.

get.description:
Single roll-up endpoint for the SPA's home page. Mirrors what
hillco-portal's /home rendered: my-stats, my open followups,
outstanding invoices, recent notes, and a compact audit feed.

Limits are intentional — this is meant to be a fast first paint, not
paginated tables. The SPA fetches the full lists from each domain's
own endpoint when the user navigates.

All users, sorted by name. Anyone authenticated can read this for
now; if the role surface grows we'll gate this on an admin role.

schema.title: Response List Users Api Admin Users Get

post.description:
Pre-authorize a new user. Until they sign in via Google OAuth
the row exists with last_login_at NULL; their first successful
OAuth callback flips that. Email is CITEXT UNIQUE — duplicates
return 409. Role gating for THIS endpoint is intentionally not
enforced yet (matches list_users); the same caveat applies.

delete.description:
Soft-delete: set is_active=false. Preserves audit_log.user_id
foreign keys and lets us reactivate later. Refuses to deactivate
the caller's own account so an admin can't lock themselves out.

post.description:
Reverse of deactivate_user. Idempotent: reactivating an already-
active user is a no-op that still returns the current row.

get.description:
Build/runtime metadata for the about/settings tab. Counts give a
quick sanity check on whether the app sees the data it should.

post.description:
Creates a draft agreement. Use PATCH to flip status='active' once
signed. services_contract auto-generates a contract_number (SC-YYYY-NNNN)
via next_contract_number(); medical_release leaves it NULL.

patch.description:
Updates an existing agreement. Status transitions are validated
only loosely here — the partial UNIQUE on active-per-type catches
the dangerous case (two active agreements of the same type for one
engagement). Use POST /agreements/{id}/supersede for the
supersession-with-new-row flow.

delete.description:
Hard delete is only permitted for draft agreements that aren't
part of a supersession chain — anything signed has financial /
legal weight and must use status transitions instead.

post.description:
Two-step move: the predecessor flips to status='superseded' and
a new draft is created with supersedes_id pointing back. Both steps
happen in the same transaction (the route's get_conn dependency)
so a partial failure rolls cleanly.

get.description:
Unified address-book list. Supports kind filter + name/email
search; returns up to 500 rows in alphabetical order. Page sizes
above that are unrealistic for a homelab CRM and would push the
SPA's table virtualization-or-pagination question we don't need
to answer yet.

Build a draft invoice from selected billable time entries and
expenses on an engagement. Either list may be empty but not both.
